structured_output.ground: Men are qawwāmūn over women (they stand in charge of them, maintaining and looking after them) because God has given some of them more than others, and because of what they spend from their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient. They guard, in the husband's absence, what God has guarded (or: they guard by means of God's guarding). As for the women whose nushūz (rising against the marriage, aversion) you fear: admonish them, leave them alone in the beds, and strike them. Then, if they obey you, do not seek a way against them. God is ever High, Great.

triggers.how: the ayah itself grounds the role in spending (bi-mā anfaqū), which is the B009 sense of qiwām: what keeps a life and a household standing
4:5 in the same surah calls wealth 'what God made a qiyām (standing, support) for you', from the same root
shared scene ritual.prayer: qunūt is 'long standing' (B002), so a second kind of standing sits in the next clause

findings.statement: Men are in charge of women, and the intensive form qawwām, 'one who stands a great deal', lets several branches be heard together: standing upright (B002), taking charge and guarding (B004), level and straight (B008), and being the prop that a thing stands on (B009). Together they describe someone whose work is to keep the household standing.
findings.perceptible: The role becomes a physical posture of holding something up, not a rank above it. Its measure is the load it carries, paid from the carrier's own wealth, and it is tied in the same sentence to what is spent.

triggers.how: concordance: only 3 uses (4:34, 4:135, 5:8). The other two are 'be qawwāmīn for justice / for God', and 4:135 is in this surah and adds 'even against yourselves'

findings.statement: The husbands are in charge, and the only other Quranic uses of the word command believers to stand firm for justice even against themselves. That role is heard inside this charge.
findings.perceptible: The household charge is measured by the same standard of justice that 4:135 applies to the person holding it. Qawwām is a duty to stand for something, not a licence.

triggers.how: shared root ق و م with qiyām in 4:5 ('your wealth which God made a support for you')
syntax: min amwālihim, 'from their wealth'

findings.statement: Men stand over the household by what they spend, and in this surah wealth is itself called the thing people stand on (4:5). The qawwām stands others up by paying out what holds him up.
findings.perceptible: Causally, the standing moves from the man's wealth to the household. The ground of his role is a transfer out of his own support.

triggers.how: second bi-mā
third bi-mā

findings.statement: The ayah gives three grounds, each introduced by bi-mā ('by / because of what'): what God preferred, what the men spend, and what God guarded. The men's standing rests on two of them and the women's guarding on the third.
findings.perceptible: Nothing in the household stands on its own. Each role is propped on a cause: two point to God's act and one to a costly human act. The structure reads as reasons for roles, not as ranks.

triggers.how: the paired part
the same phrase two ayat earlier, with the command not to covet it and to ask God for His faḍl
parts of one whole that reached each other (I11)

findings.statement: God has preferred some over others, and the text says 'some of them over some' (baʿḍahum ʿalā baʿḍ), not 'men over women'. The masculine plural pronoun can cover the whole group, so the preference is placed between parts of one body.
findings.perceptible: The relation is that of parts inside one whole, the same baʿḍ that in 4:21 reached toward the other and in 4:25 came from the other. The advantage is partial and runs between parts; it does not set one sex above the other wholesale.

triggers.how: 'ask God of His faḍl', a surplus open to every asker
misers hide what God gave them 'of His faḍl'
the next ground is spending

findings.statement: God's preference is heard beside faḍl's root image of surplus, what is left over after need (B001), and of a gift that was not owed (B003). The extra given to some is the stock from which they spend.
findings.perceptible: Faḍl and infāq read as one movement: a surplus comes in from God and goes out as spending. 4:37 shows the opposite case, a surplus that is hidden and not spent.

triggers.how: min amwālihim: a partitive 'from' their wealth
neighbouring spending done for show
spending from what God provided

findings.statement: They spend from their wealth, and the root keeps nafād (running out) and the dictionary's 'the spender grows poorer as his wealth goes' (B002) alive beside giving.
findings.perceptible: The ground of the role costs the man something; it is a depletion he carries. In the following ayat (4:36–39) this spending sits between spending for show and miserliness.

triggers.how: followed by ʿalā (4:34:3): 'over / in charge of' the women
preceded by ʿalā (4:34:9): 'some over some'
preceded by ʿalayhinna (4:34:34): 'a way against them'

findings.statement: The dictionary places the preposition ʿalā in the same root as ʿAliyy (ع ل و B012). The ayah's human 'over' appears three times (men over women, some over some, a way against them), and it closes on God, who is ʿAliyy.
findings.perceptible: The ayah is built as a vertical, and every human 'over' in it ends beneath the One who is truly high. The last word answers the first relation.

triggers.how: concordance: in 59 of 62 uses al-ṣāliḥāt names good deeds (ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāt). Here alone it names persons

findings.statement: Righteous women are named by the word the Quran almost always uses for righteous deeds. The women are described in the vocabulary of works that please God.
findings.perceptible: 'Ṣāliḥāt' is heard as a standing moral and religious quality, not a household label. It is the same word as 'those who believe and do ṣāliḥāt'.

triggers.how: shared root: the repair the arbiters seek
shared root: the settlement between spouses when the husband is the one with nushūz

findings.statement: The righteous women are ṣāliḥāt, and the same root in 4:35 and 4:128 names repair and reconciliation, removing aversion between people (B002). Nushūz is placed between these words.
findings.perceptible: The breakdown this ayah describes is framed by one root: sound people at the start and the mending (iṣlāḥ, ṣulḥ) at the end. The goal of the whole sequence is to restore what was sound.

triggers.how: a standing next to a standing
2:238 joins the same three roots: ḥāfiẓū ʿalā al-ṣalawāt … wa-qūmū lillāhi qānitīn
33:35 pairs al-qānitīn/al-qānitāt and al-ḥāfiẓīn/al-ḥāfiẓāt, the same qualities in men and women

findings.statement: The women are devoutly obedient, and qunūt keeps its senses of humble obedience in religion (B001) and long standing in prayer (B002), a word that elsewhere is standing before God.
findings.perceptible: The men stand for the household; the women stand in devotion. 2:238 uses ḥ-f-ẓ, q-w-m and q-n-t together for prayer, so these descriptions share a vocabulary of worship. 33:35 shows that the two qualities belong to believers of both sexes.

triggers.how: nominal predicate
second nominal predicate

findings.statement: 'The righteous women are qānitāt, ḥāfiẓāt' is a nominal sentence describing what such women are. It is not an imperative addressed to them, and it follows from what came before (fa-).
findings.perceptible: The women are presented as agents with qualities. The imperatives in the ayah are all addressed to the men.

triggers.how: ḥ-f-ẓ B001 guarding and B006 guarding what is sacrosanct and the covenant, chastity
the fortress image of 4:24–25 (I2)

findings.statement: They guard in the unseen, and the dictionary gives exactly the case where 'a woman is mughība when her husband is away', which includes guarding what belongs to his absence (B005).
findings.perceptible: This completes the fortress image: when the one who stands for the household is away, the one inside keeps its interior, its trust, honour and property.

triggers.how: concordance: in 32 of 49 uses ghayb is the unseen that God knows and possesses; 4:34 is one of two uses for absence
God as guard in the same clause

findings.statement: 'Ghayb' here means the husband's absence, and the word keeps its Quranic weight as the realm that only God sees.
findings.perceptible: The women's guarding happens where no husband watches and only God sees. This makes their faithfulness a matter between them and God.

triggers.how: shared root in adjacent words
God as subject

findings.statement: They guard the unseen 'by what God guarded', so the women's guarding rests on God's: He has guarded them and their rights, and He guards the walls while they keep the inside.
findings.perceptible: Two guardings are nested, the inner one human and the outer one divine. The women's role gets a cause just as the men's does (F4).

triggers.how: the verb whose subject/object changes with the reading

findings.statement: In the accusative reading 'bi-mā ḥafiẓa Allāha', the women guard the unseen by virtue of having guarded God, that is, His commands and limits. In the nominative, God guards.
findings.perceptible: The two readings make the guarding run both ways: God guards them, and they guard what is God's. (The variant data places it at 4:34:27 'فى'; it belongs to the word ٱللَّهُ at 4:34:21. The identification of the reader and the gloss are from memory.)

triggers.how: guarding the absent

findings.statement: Guarding what belongs to the husband's absence can be heard to include the absent person's name, the sphere of ghība (speaking of someone in his absence, B004).
findings.perceptible: The guarding covers speech about the absent spouse as well as property and body.

triggers.how: the next ayah begins again with fear, now of a split between the two
the wife fears nushūz from her husband

findings.statement: 'Whose nushūz you fear' uses khawf as 'expecting harm from a sign' (B001). The steps start at the first signs, before any break is complete, and the surah gives the same fear to the wife in 4:128.
findings.perceptible: The sequence is timed early, as a response to a threatened break rather than a completed one. The fear runs in both directions in the surah.

triggers.how: B002 rising from one's seat; full entry (ʿAyn): 'a mount on whose back saddle and rider do not settle', 'a heart that rises from its place in terror'; Mufradāt: 'raising herself above obedience and turning her eye from him to another'
height is answered by the One truly high

findings.statement: Nushūz is marital defiance or aversion, and its root image of raised ground and of rising up from one's place (B001, B002) stays audible. It is a partner lifting out of the shared level and no longer settling.
findings.perceptible: Spatially, one side rises out of the common place, like ground swelling up or a mount that will not let the saddle sit. The steps that follow are attempts to bring the two back to one level.

triggers.how: the only other use, and it is the husband's nushūz
the classical entries (ʿAyn, Maqāyīs, Ṣiḥāḥ) define the husband's nushūz as 'ḍarabahā wa-jafāhā', striking her and treating her coldly

findings.statement: The fear here is of the wife's nushūz, and the dictionary says nushūz belongs to either spouse (B004, Zajjāj: 'each one's aversion to the other'). Its entries define a husband's nushūz as striking and cold-shouldering her.
findings.perceptible: The ayah's limit becomes sharp. The same act that is the last permitted step here is what the dictionary calls the husband's own nushūz once it goes beyond the limit. 'Seek no way against them' marks the point where the remedy would turn into the fault.

triggers.how: same surah: 'excellent is that with which God admonishes you'
concordance: of 15 uses, God is the admonisher (or the passive refers to His admonition) in about 8, and prophets or sages in most of the rest

findings.statement: Admonish them. Waʿẓ is a reminder of consequences 'that the heart softens to' (B001), and the Quran mostly uses the word for God's and the prophets' own address.
findings.perceptible: The first step is speech aimed at softening a heart, in the manner in which God addresses people. It is not an order given from above.

triggers.how: ه ج ر B001 cutting off, by body, tongue or heart
the preposition fī: the withdrawal is located in the beds

findings.statement: Leave them in the beds: the withdrawal takes place inside the shared bed (B002, sharing one bed), not by expulsion from the house.
findings.perceptible: The second step is bodily distance inside intimacy. The place of lying together becomes the place where closeness is withheld, while the household stays whole. The escalation moves from word to body.

triggers.how: concordance: 32:16 'their sides forsake their beds (maḍājiʿ) as they call on their Lord'; 3:154 maḍājiʿ as the places where the slain lie

findings.statement: The beds are the place where one lies on one's side, and elsewhere the Quran uses the same word for the beds the devout leave at night to pray.
findings.perceptible: The bed is where people draw close to, or away from, each other and God.

triggers.how: condition that stops the sequence
prohibition that bounds it
closing reminder of who is high

findings.statement: Strike them keeps its plain sense (B001). It is the last of three steps joined by wa-, it applies only under the feared nushūz, and the next words halt it ('if they obey, seek no way against them') and cap it with God's height.
findings.perceptible: The act sits inside a frame: a condition, a sequence moving from word to body-distance to hand, a stop, and a warning. Classical jurists read it as a light, non-injuring strike and treated it as disliked. That restriction is from memory, not from the dictionary.

findings.statement: 'If they obey you' is heard beside ṭawʿ as going along willingly, the root of ṭawʿ against karh (B001), and muṭāwaʿa as agreement between two parties (B002).
findings.perceptible: The endpoint the ayah seeks is a return to willing accord, and once it is reached nothing more may be pursued.

triggers.how: object of the seeking (B001)
38:22 'baghā baʿḍunā ʿalā baʿḍ' and 38:24 'yabghī baʿḍuhum ʿalā baʿḍ' use the same baʿḍ ʿalā baʿḍ frame as 'faḍḍala … baʿḍahum ʿalā baʿḍ'

findings.statement: 'Do not seek a way against them' uses baghā as seeking (B001), and the verb's other face, overstepping and wronging (B003), is heard with it. A seeking against someone who has come back is already a transgression.
findings.perceptible: The ayah sets two kinds of 'some over some' against each other: the preference God gives, which is lawful, and a human overreaching of some over others, which is forbidden. The same verb names both the search and the wrong.

triggers.how: 'or God makes for them (lahunna) a way', an opening for women in this surah
'an evil way' (I7)

findings.statement: No way against them (ʿalayhinna): the road that God opens for women in 4:15 (lahunna) must not be turned by husbands into a road against them.
findings.perceptible: The preposition shows the direction of the road. The question becomes which road a man opens, one that leads for her or one that leads against her.

triggers.how: ك ب ر B006 greatness and kibr
rising up
the next passage condemns the swaggering and boastful

findings.statement: God is ever High and Great. Both roots also name the blameworthy human versions, ʿuluww as haughtiness (ع ل و B003) and kibr as arrogance (ك ب ر B006), so the closing names quietly return all height and greatness to God.
findings.perceptible: The ending is the answer to both kinds of rising in the ayah, the wife's nushūz and the husband's baghy. Anyone who rises above the other is set below the One to whom height belongs.

triggers.how: predicate

findings.statement: 'Kāna' with God's names expresses what God always is, not a past state ('was').
findings.perceptible: The height named at the end is permanent and present at every step of the sequence.

findings.statement: The ayah's plain terms can be heard across a terrain: a hollow that keeps what is hidden (ghayb), a swell that rises from the level (nushūz), low ground where one lies (maḍājiʿ), and the heights (ʿAliyy).
findings.perceptible: The movement of the household takes on relief: keeping in the hollow, rising out of the level, being brought back down to the shared ground, and height kept for God.

triggers.how: standing

findings.statement: 'Men' comes from the root of the leg and of going on foot (B001, B003), and the idiom 'standing on one leg' means applying oneself earnestly to a matter (B019). It sits right beside qawwāmūn.
findings.perceptible: The first two words both have a bodily sense: legs and standing.

grammar: qawwām is an intensive pattern (faʿʿāl): one who stands for something constantly or greatly, not simply one who is in charge.
baʿḍahum ʿalā baʿḍ: the masculine plural pronoun can cover a mixed group; the text says 'some of them over some', not 'them over them'.
ʿalā, 'over / against', belongs to the root of ʿAliyy according to the dictionary (ع ل و B012); the ayah's three human 'over's end in God's name ʿAliyy.
Three bi-mā clauses ground the roles: two for the men (God's preference, their spending) and one for the women (God's guarding).
fa-l-ṣāliḥātu qānitātun ḥāfiẓātun is a nominal description, not a command to the women; every imperative in the ayah is addressed to the men.
fī al-maḍājiʿ: the withdrawal happens in the beds, not by putting her out of the house.
fa-in aṭaʿnakum fa-lā tabghū: a condition with an immediate prohibition that stops the sequence.
kāna with God's names means 'is ever', not 'was'.
variants: bi-mā ḥafiẓa Allāha (accusative, a canonical reading): 'by their having guarded God('s commands)' beside the common 'by what God guarded'. The guarding runs both ways, from God to them and from them to God. The data attaches it to 4:34:27; it belongs to ٱللَّهُ at 4:34:21.
structured_output.reread: A household stands because someone holds it up. The men are qawwāmūn, 'those who stand much' for it, and the only other uses of the word call believers to stand for justice even against themselves. Their standing rests on two grounds: a surplus God gave 'some over some' within one body, and the wealth they pay out. In this surah wealth is itself what people stand on, so the man keeps others standing with his own support. The women have their own standing. They are ṣāliḥāt, the word for good deeds; they are qānitāt, standing long before God; and they are ḥāfiẓāt, keeping the inside of the house and their honour in the husband's absence, in the realm only God sees, resting on God's own guarding. If one side begins to rise out of the common level (nushūz, raised ground; and the surah says it can be the husband who rises, 4:128), the remedy moves from a heart-softening word, to distance within the very bed, to the hand. Then it stops. Once there is accord, any 'way against them' becomes baghy, the overreaching of some over some, and in the classical dictionary the husband's own nushūz is 'striking her and treating her coldly'. The ayah is built from three human 'over's (ʿalā), and the last word, ʿAliyy, takes every height back: only God is truly high and great. The next ayah sends envoys to fit the two together again.

set_aside.what: ض ر ب B002 (travelling, going away), B004 (withholding, keeping to the house), B005 (restraining the hand), B006 (casting a covering), B003 (striking an example)
set_aside.why: The plan asks not to force a latent branch onto iḍribūhunna. None of these is activated by the ayah's words: B002 needs fī al-arḍ, B003 needs mathal, and with a direct personal object the concordance places this use among 'striking a person'. Modern proposals of 'separate' or 'withhold' readings are from memory and not supported by triggers here. The image works through the frame instead (F20, F24, F26, F28).

set_aside.what: ه ج ر B003 (hujr, foul speech: 'speak harshly to them')
set_aside.why: The imperative uhjurū is the form of hajr (leaving). A reading as harsh speech would need a different verb form; it is known only from memory of tafsir discussion.
